simple.meaning: מַשְׂכֹּרֶת (maskôreth) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “wages or a reward.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Genesis, Ruth, beginning at Genesis 29:15. Its contexts include family, family line, flock, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַשְׂכֹּרֶת (H4909).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַשְׂכֹּרֶת (maskôreth) / H4909 is traced through Genesis 29:15, Genesis 31:7, Genesis 31:41, Ruth 2:12 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Laban said to Jacob, “Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what will your wages be?”

timeline.evidenceText: Laban said to Jacob, “Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what will your wages be?”
Your father has deceived me, and changed my wages ten times, but God didn’t allow him to hurt me.
These twenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed my wages ten times.
May Yahweh repay your work, and a full reward be given to you from Yahweh, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”
